title: Preserve local rubric wording and separate run-in labels
body:
Repeated rubric identities now keep the wording printed at the selected occurrence, with the existing project/language fallback for occurrences that supply no local wording. This prevents one edition’s instructions from replacing another occurrence’s text.

Run-in instruction and description labels also get a separating space before an adjacent word or inline text element. For example, the Musaf label “הש״ץ בקול” remains separate from “כהנים”; existing whitespace and punctuation stay intact. The electronic renderer emits a real text space too, so copied text and screen readers retain the same word boundary.

Validation: 379 stylesheet tests and 161 subtests pass on this branch; 379 tests and 161 subtests pass in the combined maḥzor export runtime. All 176 electronic-export tests and 182 subtests pass in both worktrees. Found during the final scan294–311 review for #214. Kept separate from the digitization PR #296.

Parallel copies now preserve that trailing boundary before the rubric is detached from its paragraph. A bilingual regression reproduces the actual Musaf failure; the real compiled documentary paragraphs also contain the required separators.
